Alyssa — appreciate the clarity. Quick responses and a compromise we think will address finance and procurement concerns:

- Burst handling: overage in any month will be invoiced monthly at the applicable per-token/seat rate; at annual reconciliation we will apply credits such that total billed will not exceed the annual cap. Example: if a single month is 3x baseline, that month is billed as normal; if annual spend exceeds the cap, payments above the cap will be credited backward at reconciliation. I'll attach a worked example in Exhibit-D v2.
- Monthly floor shortfalls: floor guarantees are annualized (i.e., floors aggregated over 12 months). A short month counts toward the annual floor; no carry-forward credits month-to-month but the annual reconciliation will reflect aggregate.
- Amortization: we are open to 9 months for onboarding credits for ARR accounting reasons; suggest 9 months as you asked.
- Billing window: we can accept a 45-day limit on raising overage invoices as long as both parties agree that usage reports provided monthly start the clock.

Next steps: Laura from Customer Success can confirm the onboarding milestones tie to amortization; Markus (cc'd) will draft lean legal language for the order form so you have something to redline. I'll send Exhibit-D v2 with an example calculation by EOD.

Thanks — want to get this across the finish line this week.
Ben

Subject: Re: Fee amortization & collar — legal redlines (draft)

Alyssa / Ben — attaching a concise redline to the Order Form (OrderForm_RWI-AstroGrid_v3_redline.docx). High-level legal positions we propose:

1) Fee Collar: define "Annual Floor" and "Annual Cap" as monetary amounts measured on a rolling 12 month basis from the Effective Date. Tether the cap relief to the 95th percentile of monthly usage in the prior 12 months to avoid one-off anomalies driving the cap.

2) Amortization: onboarding credits shall be amortized over nine (9) months, and credits shall not result in a negative invoice. If Customer terminates before the amortization period completes for convenience, unamortized credits will be accelerated and netted against final invoices.

3) Billing/Notice: Provider must issue overage invoices within forty-five (45) days of issuing the monthly usage report. Customer must raise disputes within thirty (30) days of invoice receipt.

4) Remedies/Overages: for material sustained overage (defined as three consecutive months >150% of committed monthly average), Provider reserves the right to require conversion to a higher committed band upon 60 days written notice. We can make this a mutual trigger with a good-faith cure period.

I kept the redline focused on principles — happy to soften the percentile, notice periods, or the cure mechanics to get to signature.

Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
